ordering_tiers.tier_1: Baseline — ordered for every new patient
ordering_tiers.tier_2: Expanded — ordered based on tier_1 results or hallmark activation
ordering_tiers.tier_3: Specialty — ordered based on tier_2 results or specific clinical indication

_metadata.source_notes: Evidence-based ranges from Tietz 5th ed + longevity-optimal overlays. Hallmark associations based on Lopez-Otin et al. 2023 Hallmarks of Aging framework.

biomarkers.notes: Core electrolyte. Part of CMP. Dysnatremia indicates fluid/electrolyte imbalance.
Critical electrolyte for cardiac and muscle function. Part of CMP.
Electrolyte balance marker. Part of CMP. Used in anion gap calculation.
Acid-base balance marker. Low bicarbonate may indicate metabolic acidosis.
Kidney function marker. Elevated BUN may indicate dehydration or renal impairment.
Primary kidney function marker. Sex-specific ranges. Part of CMP.
Fasting glucose. Part of CMP. Key metabolic marker.
Bone and metabolic health marker. Part of CMP.
Nutritional and liver function marker. Part of CMP.
Key nutritional and liver function marker. PhenoAge component. Low albumin predicts mortality.
Liver function marker. Part of CMP. Mild elevation may have antioxidant properties.
Liver-specific enzyme. Optimal: <25 (M), <20 (F). Part of CMP.
Liver and muscle enzyme. Part of CMP. Elevated in liver disease and muscle injury.
Liver/bone enzyme. PhenoAge component. Part of CMP.
Kidney filtration rate. Calculated from creatinine. Part of CMP.
Fasting glucose. ADA: <100 normal, 100-125 prediabetes, ≥126 diabetes.
Hyperinsulinemia reflects mTOR/insulin/IGF-1 axis overactivation. Optimal <5 uIU/mL.
3-month average glucose. ADA: <5.7% normal, 5.7-6.4% prediabetes, ≥6.5% diabetes.

aliases: Homeostatic Model Assessment of Insulin Resistance
biomarkers.notes: Calculated: (fasting glucose × fasting insulin) / 405. Optimal <1.0.
Gout and metabolic syndrome marker. Optimal: <5.5 (M), <4.5 (F). Elevated in insulin resistance.
Endogenous insulin production marker. Distinguishes T1D from T2D.
Tissue damage marker. Elevated in hemolysis, liver disease, cancer.
Bone and energy metabolism marker. Part of CMP.
Cofactor for 300+ enzymes. Serum levels poorly reflect intracellular stores.
Liver/oxidative stress marker. Optimal: <20 (M), <15 (F). Sensitive to alcohol.
PhenoAge component. Elevated WBC associated with higher mortality. Optimal 4.5-7.0.
Red cell count. Part of CBC.
Oxygen-carrying capacity. Sex-specific ranges. Part of CBC.
Percentage of blood volume occupied by red cells. Part of CBC.
PhenoAge component. Macrocytosis suggests B12/folate deficiency or liver disease.
Average hemoglobin per red cell. Part of CBC.
Hemoglobin concentration per red cell. Part of CBC.
PhenoAge component. Elevated RDW is a strong mortality predictor.
Clotting and inflammation marker. Part of CBC.
Primary innate immune cells. Elevated in infection/inflammation.
Adaptive immune cells. Low lymphocytes indicate immunosenescence.
Innate immune cells. Elevated in chronic inflammation.
Elevated in allergic conditions and parasitic infections.
Rare granulocytes. Elevated in myeloproliferative disorders.
Neutrophil fraction of WBC differential.
PhenoAge component. Low lymphocyte % associated with higher mortality.
Immature red cells. Reflects bone marrow erythropoietic activity.
Serum iron. Diurnal variation; best drawn fasting AM.
Reflects transferrin capacity. Elevated in iron deficiency.
Iron/TIBC ratio. Elevated in hemochromatosis, low in iron deficiency.
Iron storage marker. Optimal: M 70-150, F 50-100 ng/mL. Also acute phase reactant.
Functional iron deficiency marker. Not affected by inflammation unlike ferritin.
Standard lipid panel. Desirable <200 mg/dL.
Primary cardiovascular risk marker. ACC/AHA 2018 guidelines.
Protective lipoprotein. Optimal: M >60, F >70 mg/dL.
Fasting triglycerides. Optimal <80 mg/dL for longevity.
Calculated from triglycerides/5. Reflects hepatic lipid output.
Total cholesterol minus HDL. Better predictor than LDL-C alone.
Primary driver of atherosclerosis. Preferred over LDL-C for cardiovascular risk.
Major HDL protein. Higher levels protective. ApoB/ApoA1 ratio is a risk metric.
Genetically determined. Major independent cardiovascular risk factor. Measure once.
NMR-measured LDL particle number. Better predictor than LDL-C in insulin resistance.
NMR-measured HDL particle number. Higher is protective.
Small dense LDL particles are more atherogenic. Larger size is protective.
Vascular inflammation marker. Predicts coronary artery disease risk.
Systemic inflammation marker. AHA/CDC: <1.0 low, 1-3 average, >3 high CV risk.
Coagulation and inflammation marker. Elevated in cardiovascular risk.
One-carbon metabolism marker. Elevated in B12/folate deficiency. CV and dementia risk.
Heart failure and cardiac stress marker. Age-adjusted thresholds apply.
Cardiac injury marker. High-sensitivity assay detects subclinical myocardial stress.
Cardiac injury marker. Roche Elecsys assay. Elevated in subclinical cardiac stress.
Clot formation/dissolution marker. Elevated in thrombosis, inflammation.
Extrinsic coagulation pathway. Prolonged in liver disease, vitamin K deficiency.
Standardized PT ratio. Therapeutic range 2-3 for anticoagulation.
Intrinsic coagulation pathway. Prolonged in hemophilia, lupus anticoagulant.
Neutrophil-derived oxidative enzyme. Predicts cardiovascular events.
Oxidatively modified LDL. Highly atherogenic. Reflects oxidative stress.
Most atherogenic LDL subfraction. Elevated in metabolic syndrome.
Comprehensive lipoprotein subfraction analysis. Identifies atherogenic patterns.
EPA+DHA as % of total RBC fatty acids. >8% clinical target, >10% optimal.
Draw AM (7-10am). Optimal 600-900 ng/dL for longevity. Declines ~1%/year after 30.
Biologically active testosterone fraction. More clinically relevant than total T.
Free + albumin-bound testosterone. Calculated from total T, SHBG, albumin.
Binds testosterone and estradiol. High SHBG reduces free testosterone.
Potent androgen. Elevated in BPH and androgenic alopecia.
Pituitary hormone stimulating testosterone production. Elevated in primary hypogonadism.
Pituitary hormone. Elevated in primary testicular failure.
Estrogen in males. Optimal 20-30 pg/mL. Elevated in obesity/aromatase excess.
Elevated prolactin suppresses testosterone. Rule out pituitary adenoma.
Adrenal androgen. Declines with age. Optimal 200-400 ug/dL for longevity.
Draw 7-9am. Optimal 10-18 ug/dL. Chronic elevation drives catabolism and aging.
Draw 3-5pm. Should be <50% of AM value. Elevated PM cortisol indicates HPA dysregulation.
Mother hormone. Precursor to all steroid hormones. Declines with age.
GH surrogate. U-shaped mortality. Optimal 150-250 ng/mL (adult). Age-dependent.
Major IGF-1 carrier protein. Modulates IGF-1 bioavailability.
Pulsatile secretion. Random GH not clinically useful; use IGF-1 as surrogate.
Prostate cancer screening. Age-specific thresholds. Velocity >0.75 ng/mL/yr is concerning.
Free/total PSA ratio. <10% high cancer risk, 10-25% intermediate, >25% low risk.
Sertoli cell marker. Reflects spermatogenesis and testicular function.
Duplicate of shbg for male-specific panel context. See shbg.
Adrenal androgen precursor. Elevated in CAH and PCOS.
Progesterone in males. Precursor to cortisol and testosterone.
Female testosterone. Low levels associated with low libido, fatigue, muscle loss.
Free testosterone in females. Elevated in PCOS.
Higher in females than males. Low SHBG in PCOS/insulin resistance.
Cycle-dependent. Follicular: 2.4-12.6, Ovulatory: 14-95, Luteal: 1-11.4 mIU/mL.
Cycle-dependent. Elevated FSH (>25) indicates diminished ovarian reserve/menopause.
Cycle-dependent. Follicular: 12-166, Luteal: 43-228, Postmeno: <6 pg/mL.
Dominant estrogen in postmenopause. Produced from androstenedione in adipose tissue.
Cycle-dependent. Follicular: <1, Luteal: 2-25 ng/mL. Confirms ovulation.
Elevated in pituitary adenoma, hypothyroidism. Suppresses ovulation.
Adrenal androgen. Elevated in PCOS. Declines with age.
Draw 7-9am. Optimal 10-18 ug/dL.
Ovarian reserve marker. Declines with age. Not cycle-dependent.
Granulosa cell marker. Reflects follicular pool. Declines in perimenopause.
GH surrogate. Age-dependent. Optimal 150-250 ng/mL (adult).
Mother hormone. Precursor to all steroid hormones.
Adrenal androgen. Elevated in PCOS and CAH.
DUTCH test. Measures cortisol metabolites (THF, THE, allo-THF). Reflects total cortisol production.
DUTCH test. 2-OHE1/16-OHE1 ratio. Favorable: higher 2-OH pathway. Cancer risk assessment.
DUTCH test. Pregnanediol and allopregnanolone metabolites.
DUTCH test. Androsterone, etiocholanolone, DHEA metabolites.
DUTCH test. Melatonin metabolite. Reflects circadian rhythm and sleep quality.
DUTCH test OAT markers: B12, B6, glutathione, melatonin, oxidative stress markers.
Composite flag for PCOS workup: testosterone, DHEA-S, LH/FSH ratio, insulin, AMH.
Composite flag: FSH >25, estradiol <6, AMH <0.5. Confirms menopause.
Composite flag for perimenopause: irregular cycles, FSH variability, AMH decline.
Pregnancy hormone. Also elevated in gestational trophoblastic disease.
Primary thyroid screening. Optimal 1.0-2.5 mIU/L for longevity.
Active thyroid hormone. Optimal 3.2-4.2 pg/mL. Low in hypothyroidism and poor T4-T3 conversion.
Prohormone. Optimal 1.1-1.6 ng/dL. Converted to active T3.
Inactive T3 metabolite. Elevated in stress, illness, low-calorie diets.
Total T3 (bound + free). Less useful than free T3 for functional assessment.
Total T4. Affected by binding protein changes. Free T4 preferred.
Hashimoto's thyroiditis marker. Elevated in autoimmune thyroid disease.
Autoimmune thyroid marker. Also interferes with thyroglobulin tumor marker.
Thyroid cancer surveillance marker. Undetectable after thyroidectomy is goal.
Thyroid hormone transport protein. Elevated by estrogen, decreased by androgens.
Systemic inflammation. Optimal <0.5 mg/L for longevity.
Master pro-inflammatory cytokine. SASP component. Drives inflammaging.
Master pro-inflammatory cytokine. Elevated in chronic inflammation and SASP.
Non-specific inflammation marker. Optimal <10 mm/hr for longevity.
Ferritin as acute phase reactant. Very high levels indicate systemic inflammation.
Central complement protein. Low in autoimmune disease, high in metabolic syndrome.
Classical complement pathway. Low in SLE and hereditary angioedema.
Autoimmune screening. Positive ≥1:80. Reflex to specific antibodies if positive.
Specific for SLE. Correlates with disease activity and lupus nephritis.
Innate immune surveillance. Low NK cells associated with cancer risk and immunosenescence.
NK cell fraction of lymphocytes.
Adaptive immune function. Low in HIV, immunosenescence.
Cytotoxic T cells. Elevated in chronic viral infections and immunosenescence.
Immune balance marker. Low ratio in HIV, immunosenescence. Optimal 1.5-2.5.
Comprehensive T, B, NK cell enumeration by flow cytometry.
Primary antibody class. Low in immunodeficiency, high in chronic infection/autoimmune.
Mucosal immunity antibody. Low in selective IgA deficiency.
First antibody in immune response. Elevated in Waldenström macroglobulinemia.
Neutrophil-derived inflammation marker. Elevated in systemic inflammation.
Acute phase reactant and coagulation factor. Elevated in chronic inflammation.
Optimal 50-80 ng/mL for longevity. Endocrine Society: >30 sufficient.
Optimal 500-900 pg/mL. Deficiency causes neurological damage and megaloblastic anemia.
One-carbon metabolism. Optimal >10 ng/mL. Critical for methylation and DNA synthesis.
Reflects long-term folate status (3-month average). More stable than serum folate.
Cofactor for 100+ enzymes. Critical for homocysteine metabolism.
FAD/FMN precursor. Critical for mitochondrial electron transport chain.
Pyruvate dehydrogenase cofactor. Deficiency causes Wernicke encephalopathy.
Vision, immune function, gene expression. Toxicity possible at high doses.
Fat-soluble antioxidant. Protects cell membranes from oxidative damage.
Activates osteocalcin and matrix Gla protein. Bone and vascular calcification prevention.
Better reflects intracellular magnesium than serum. Optimal 5.5-6.8 mg/dL.
Immune function, DNA repair, antioxidant defense. Optimal 90-120 ug/dL.
Cofactor for SOD, cytochrome c oxidase. Zinc/copper ratio important.
Glutathione peroxidase cofactor. Antioxidant and thyroid function. Optimal 110-150 ng/mL.
Insulin sensitizer. Deficiency associated with glucose intolerance.
Cofactor for xanthine oxidase and sulfite oxidase. Rare deficiency.
MnSOD cofactor. Mitochondrial antioxidant defense.
Thyroid hormone precursor. WHO: <100 ug/L deficient, 100-199 adequate.
Mitochondrial electron transport chain component. Depleted by statins. Optimal 1.0-2.5 ug/mL.
EPA+DHA as % of total RBC fatty acids. >8% clinical, >10% optimal.
Inflammatory balance. Western diet: 15-20:1. Optimal <4:1 for longevity.
Anti-inflammatory omega-3. Precursor to resolvins and protectins.
Brain and retinal omega-3. Critical for neurological function.
Fatty acid transport into mitochondria. Deficiency impairs beta-oxidation.
Free (unbound) carnitine. Reflects available carnitine for fatty acid transport.
Conditionally essential amino acid. Declines with age. Longevity research interest.
Universal antioxidant. Regenerates vitamins C and E. Mitochondrial cofactor.
Master antioxidant. Declines with age. Critical for detoxification.
Sirtuin activator. Declines with age. Critical for mitochondrial function and DNA repair.
NAD+ precursor. Deficiency causes pellagra. Important for energy metabolism.
CoA precursor. Essential for fatty acid synthesis and energy metabolism.
Carboxylase cofactor. Histone biotinylation. Interferes with many immunoassays.
Methyl donor. Phosphatidylcholine synthesis. Liver and brain function.
Insulin signaling second messenger. Used in PCOS treatment.
Methyl donor. Homocysteine remethylation. Liver protection.
Liver-specific enzyme. Optimal: <25 (M), <20 (F). Elevated in NAFLD, hepatitis.
Liver and muscle enzyme. AST/ALT ratio >2 suggests alcoholic liver disease.
Sensitive liver marker. Elevated by alcohol, medications, NAFLD.
Cholestasis and bone marker. Elevated in biliary obstruction, Paget's disease.
Liver function and hemolysis marker. Jaundice when >2.5 mg/dL.
Conjugated bilirubin. Elevated in hepatocellular disease and cholestasis.
Unconjugated bilirubin. Elevated in hemolysis and Gilbert syndrome.
Liver synthetic function marker. Low in cirrhosis, malnutrition, inflammation.
Liver synthetic function. Includes albumin and globulins.
Tissue damage marker. Elevated in liver disease, hemolysis, cancer.
Liver synthetic function. Prolonged INR indicates severe liver dysfunction.
Hepatic encephalopathy marker. Elevated in liver failure and urea cycle disorders.
Kidney filtration marker. Sex-specific ranges. Affected by muscle mass.
Kidney function and protein catabolism marker. BUN/Cr ratio >20 suggests prerenal azotemia.
Better GFR marker than creatinine. Not affected by muscle mass. Optimal <0.8 mg/L.
GFR estimated from cystatin C. More accurate in elderly and low muscle mass.
Gout and kidney stone risk. Hyperuricemia associated with CKD progression.
Early kidney damage marker. KDIGO: <30 A1, 30-300 A2, >300 A3.
Total proteinuria marker. >500 mg/g indicates significant proteinuria.
Elevated in CKD. Hyperphosphatemia drives vascular calcification.
Calcium-phosphorus product important in CKD. Hypocalcemia in advanced CKD.
Intestinal inflammation marker. Elevated in IBD. Distinguishes IBD from IBS.
Exocrine pancreatic function. <200 ug/g indicates pancreatic insufficiency.
Intestinal permeability marker. Elevated in leaky gut. Controversial assay.
Mucosal immune defense. Low sIgA indicates mucosal immune deficiency.
H. pylori infection. Positive requires eradication therapy. Gastric cancer risk.
Gold standard non-invasive H. pylori test. Used for test-of-cure.
Small intestinal bacterial overgrowth. >20 ppm rise positive.
Intestinal methanogen overgrowth (IMO). Associated with constipation-predominant IBS.
Intestinal permeability assessment. Elevated ratio indicates leaky gut.
Primary colonocyte fuel. HDAC inhibitor. Anti-inflammatory and anti-cancer.
SCFA. Gluconeogenesis substrate. Satiety signaling.
Most abundant SCFA. Energy substrate for peripheral tissues.
Sum of butyrate, propionate, acetate. Reflects microbiome fermentation capacity.
Deconjugates estrogens and toxins. Elevated increases estrogen recirculation.
Systemic inflammation from gut origin. Correlates with intestinal inflammation.
PCR-based stool pathogen panel. Detects bacteria, parasites, viruses, fungi.
Higher diversity associated with better health outcomes. Declines with age.
Composite score of pathobiont/commensal ratio. Higher score indicates dysbiosis.
CDC: <5 ug/dL reference. No safe level. Neurotoxic, nephrotoxic.
Neurotoxin. Sources: fish, dental amalgam. Optimal <3 ug/L.
Carcinogen. Sources: groundwater, rice, seafood. Speciation important.
Nephrotoxin and carcinogen. Sources: cigarettes, contaminated food.
Neurotoxin. Accumulates in CKD. Sources: antacids, cookware.
Carcinogen. Sources: stainless steel, jewelry, food.
Sources: canned foods, dental materials. Organotin compounds are toxic.
Highly toxic. Sources: coal burning, cement production.
Hexavalent chromium is carcinogenic. Sources: industrial exposure, implants.
Sources: metal-on-metal implants, industrial exposure. Cardiomyopathy risk.
Potent hepatocarcinogen. Sources: moldy grains, nuts. IARC Group 1.
Nephrotoxic mycotoxin. Sources: moldy grains, coffee, wine.
Immunosuppressive mycotoxin. Sources: Fusarium mold in grains.
Estrogenic mycotoxin. Sources: Fusarium mold. Endocrine disruptor.
Aspergillus fumigatus toxin. Immunosuppressive. Marker of invasive aspergillosis.
Endocrine disruptor. Sources: plastics, canned food linings.
Endocrine disruptor. Sources: PVC plastics, medical devices.
DEP metabolite. Sources: personal care products, fragrances.
Forever chemical. Carcinogen. Sources: non-stick cookware, food packaging.
Forever chemical. Immunotoxic. Sources: firefighting foam, stain-resistant products.
PFAS compound. Thyroid disruption. Sources: food packaging.
PFAS compound. Sources: firefighting foam, stain-resistant products.
Benzene exposure marker. Leukemogen. Sources: gasoline, cigarettes.
Toluene exposure marker. Sources: paints, adhesives, gasoline.
Xylene exposure marker. Sources: paints, varnishes, cleaning agents.
Styrene exposure marker. Sources: plastics, rubber, food packaging.
Acrylamide exposure. Sources: fried/baked starchy foods, cigarettes. Neurotoxin.
Herbicide. IARC Group 2A probable carcinogen. Sources: non-organic food.
Herbicide. Parkinson's disease risk. Mitochondrial complex I inhibitor.
Cholinesterase inhibitors. Sources: pesticides, insecticides. Neurotoxic.
Prostate cancer screening. Age-specific ranges. Velocity and density important.
Colorectal, lung, breast cancer marker. Elevated in smokers. Used for monitoring.
Ovarian cancer marker. Also elevated in endometriosis, fibroids. Used for monitoring.
Pancreatic, biliary, colorectal cancer marker. Not useful for screening.
Hepatocellular carcinoma, germ cell tumor marker. Elevated in cirrhosis.
Breast cancer monitoring marker. Not for screening. Used to track treatment response.
Germ cell tumor marker. Elevated in testicular cancer, choriocarcinoma.
Gastric, colorectal, ovarian cancer marker. Used for monitoring.
Non-small cell lung cancer marker. Cytokeratin 19 fragment.
Small cell lung cancer, neuroblastoma marker. Also elevated in hemolysis.
Melanoma monitoring marker. Also brain injury marker. Glial cell protein.
Neuroendocrine tumor marker. Elevated in carcinoid, pheochromocytoma. PPI use elevates.
Medullary thyroid cancer marker. Elevated in MEN2. Calcium stimulation test.
Differentiated thyroid cancer monitoring. Should be undetectable post-thyroidectomy.
Multi-cancer early detection via cell-free DNA methylation. Detects 50+ cancer types.
Best mortality predictor among epigenetic clocks. Trained on time-to-death. Acceleration = biological age - chronological age.
Rate of biological aging. 1.0 = average pace. <1.0 = slower aging. Responsive to interventions.
First-generation epigenetic clock. 353 CpG sites. Pan-tissue applicability.
Blood-specific epigenetic clock. 71 CpG sites. Correlates with age-related diseases.
Trained on phenotypic age (clinical biomarkers). Strong mortality predictor.
Telomere/single copy gene ratio. Shorter telomeres = accelerated aging. High variability.
Cellular senescence biomarker. Increases with age. Tumor suppressor. Research use.
Biological age minus chronological age. Negative = younger than expected. Key longevity metric.
Alzheimer's and cardiovascular risk. e4/e4 = 8-12x AD risk. e2/e2 = protective.
Methylation pathway variant. TT homozygous = 70% reduced enzyme activity. Folate/B12 supplementation.
Methylation pathway variant. Compound heterozygous with C677T increases risk.
Dopamine/estrogen metabolism. Met/Met = slow COMT, higher dopamine, estrogen accumulation.
Metabolizes 25% of drugs. Poor/IM/EM/UM phenotypes. Affects opioids, antidepressants, tamoxifen.
Metabolizes clopidogrel, PPIs, antidepressants. Poor metabolizers at cardiovascular risk.
Metabolizes ~50% of drugs. Statins, immunosuppressants, many others. Inducible.
Hereditary breast/ovarian cancer risk. Pathogenic variants require genetic counseling.
LDL receptor regulation. Loss-of-function = very low LDL, CV protection. Gain-of-function = FH.
Obesity risk variant. AA homozygous = 1.67x obesity risk. Modifiable by exercise.
Muscle fiber type. XX = no alpha-actinin-3, better endurance. RR = power/sprint advantage.
Comprehensive PGx panel. Includes CYP2D6, CYP2C19, CYP3A4, CYP2C9, DPYD, TPMT, UGT1A1.
Comprehensive metabolic panel. Assesses mitochondrial function, nutrient status, gut dysbiosis.
Essential and non-essential amino acids. Identifies deficiencies and metabolic disorders.
Saturated, monounsaturated, polyunsaturated fatty acids. Omega-3/6 balance.
Serotonin, dopamine, norepinephrine metabolites. Mood, cognition, sleep assessment.
4-point salivary cortisol + DHEA. Assesses HPA axis function and adrenal fatigue.

aliases: Dried Urine Test for Comprehensive Hormones
biomarkers.notes: Comprehensive sex hormones, cortisol, melatonin, organic acids. Dried urine collection.
Diurnal cortisol pattern. Morning peak, evening nadir. Assesses HPA axis rhythm.
Adrenal androgen. Declines with age. Cortisol/DHEA ratio reflects stress resilience.
Sleep hormone. Antioxidant. Declines with age. Circadian rhythm marker.
Mood, gut motility, sleep. 90% produced in gut. Reflects peripheral serotonin.
Motivation, reward, movement. Precursor to norepinephrine. Kidney dopamine production.
Stress response, alertness. Elevated in pheochromocytoma, chronic stress.
Fight-or-flight hormone. Elevated in pheochromocytoma, acute stress.
Serotonin metabolite. Elevated in carcinoid tumors. 24-hour urine collection.
Dopamine metabolite. Elevated in neuroblastoma, pheochromocytoma.
Epinephrine/norepinephrine metabolite. Elevated in pheochromocytoma, neuroblastoma.
Pyrrole disorder marker. Depletes zinc and B6. Associated with anxiety, depression.
Functional B12 deficiency marker. Elevated before serum B12 drops. Mitochondrial marker.
Methylation and cardiovascular risk marker. Optimal <8 umol/L. B12/folate/B6 dependent.
Kidney stone risk. Elevated in hyperoxaluria, gut dysbiosis, high oxalate diet.
Regulates calcium/phosphorus. Elevated PTH with low vitamin D indicates secondary hyperparathyroidism.
Reflects hydration status and electrolyte balance. Calculated: 2×Na + glucose/18 + BUN/2.8.
